summary: Ephemeral runner unable to decrypt release SSH keys during Vault transit rekey causing nightly release queue to back up
description:
Issue summary: During an automated Vault transit key rekey that started at ~2026-03-10T02:15Z, a subset of ephemeral GitLab CI runners failed to decrypt ephemeral SSH keys used for artifact publish and deploy steps. This caused the nightly release pipeline to stall and backlog ~120 jobs over the 3-hour window. Impact: Releases were delayed; some deploy jobs were marked as 'stalled' and required manual restart. Not all runners were impacted — only those whose local runner cache pointed to pre-rekey wrapped keys while Vault's replica in us-west began serving new key IDs.

Why this is unusual: The rekey is supposed to be transparent — wrapped keys are re-enciphered by Vault without breaking running clients. Here we observed a coordination gap between the Vault transit rewrap and runner-side cache validation that produced decryption errors for ephemeral key unwrap calls.
steps_to_reproduce: Schedule an automated transit rekey on primary Vault cluster (simulate by rotating transit key for 'release-ssh' keyring).
Trigger a pool of ephemeral GitLab CI runners (ephemeral-runner group) that fetch wrapped SSH keys from Vault and cache them in-memory for the job lifetime.
While some runners hold cached wrapped keys, replicate the Vault change to a region replica and update the key id served by the replica (introduce artificial replication latency ~10-30s).
Start release pipeline jobs that attempt to unwrap keys against the replica — observe decryption failures on runners with cached pre-rekey wrapped material.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:19:12Z runner-ephemeral-7f8d ERROR unwrap failed: vault transit decryption failed: key not found (kid=0x7d)
2026-03-10T02:19:13Z runner-ephemeral-3b2a ERROR deploy: ssh: failed to add key: unwrap error: encrypted key rejected
vault-primary: 2026-03-10T02:15:21Z INFO transit: starting rekey operation, new_kid=0x8a
vault-replica-us-west: 2026-03-10T02:15:35Z INFO transit: new_kid visible on replica (lag ~14s)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: rekey made wrapped keys incompatible with older replicas. Secondary hypothesis: runner cache validation failed to refresh when unwrap returned 'key not found' and retried with the same wrapped payload instead of fetching fresh wrapped key from Vault.

Checked Vault audit logs: primary successfully changed transit KID; replicas reported propagation within 10-20s depending on internal raft latencies. No Vault errors other than expected rekey messages.

Runner telemetry: affected runners showed identical behavior — they attempted to unwrap the wrapped blob multiple times without performing a 'refresh' fetch from secrets backend. The runner unwrap client treats unwrap failure as transient and retries unwrap rather than re-fetching the wrapped payload.

We observed a race: if runner fetched a wrapped key shortly before rekey, and the replica served a different KID on unwrap request, unwrap fails. If runner then retries unwrap without fetching new wrapped payload, it never recovers.
Reproducible in staging by introducing a 15s replica lag and issuing rekey while runners fetch and cache wrapped keys.
proposed_fix: Short-term: update runner unwrap flow to treat 'key not found' errors as a signal to re-fetch the wrapped payload from Vault and then retry unwrap (hotfix to runner image). Long-term: add conditional validation headers and KID-binding to cache TTL logic, and add a small jitter/refresh window on ephemeral key caching so cached wrapped material is re-validated on first unwrap failure.
workaround: Manual: Restarting the affected ephemeral runners clears in-memory cache, causing them to re-fetch current wrapped keys from Vault replicas and succeed. Operational runbook step added: for stalled release pipelines during Vault rekey, use 'ci-runner restart --selector=ephemeral-runner' as temporary mitigation. Also, temporarily pause automated rekeys during high-volume release windows.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11: Deployed runner hotfix v2026.03.11-hotfix1 that treats 'transit key not found' as cache-invalidating error and re-fetches wrapped payload before retrying unwrap. Verified in canary (20 runners) — unwrap success rate returned to 100% for rekey window. 2026-03-12: Rollout completed to all ephemeral-runner pools. Added temporary rekey blackout for scheduled release windows in Vault ops runbook.
comments: Aisha Khan (2026-03-10): Raised alert from release-nightly SRE dashboard, blocking release train. Triage assigned to Diego.
Diego Marquez (2026-03-10): Captured runner logs and confirmed pattern. Escalating to infra-runner team and Vault ops. Created staging reproducer.

Priya Sethi (Vault ops) (2026-03-10): Confirmed transit rekey occurred as scheduled. Replica lag observed ~10-18s due to leader snapshot compaction during rekey window. Working on improving replica propagation metric alerts.
Liam O'Connor (Runner eng) (2026-03-11): Implemented hotfix branch to invalidate cached wrapped keys on 'key not found' unwrap response. Preparing canary.
Diego Marquez (2026-03-12): Hotfix rolled out; monitoring. Added runbook entry and scheduled follow-up retro with Vault and Runner teams to design safer rotation windows.
